conventions.convention: The ALE map extends C² to a space-time neighborhood and is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism on neighborhoods of the closures; J=det(DξA)>0 and mesh velocity is ∂tA composed with A⁻¹.

Dimension one uses finitely many intervals with pairwise disjoint closures and endpoint normals −1 on the left and +1 on the right. The higher-dimensional Reynolds theorem assumes Countable Choice and a transported finite piecewise-C¹ boundary presentation.
Faces are periodic modulo a fixed physical period L; J is physical cell width divided by Δξ. Relative speed is c=a−w, with c⁺=max(c,0) and c⁻=min(c,0).

A nonpositive new Jacobian returns mesh_crossing without an updated state. Conservation and constant preservation require success but no CFL condition; monotonicity and weighted L1 contraction additionally require the stated cellwise CFL bound.

Both subdomains use the same real inner-product trace space Λ with dim Λ≥1. M_i and A_i are self-adjoint positive definite; outward algebraic flux is q_i=S_iλ_i−f_i, and monolithic coupling imposes equal traces and q_1+q_2=0.
Robin vector and operator norms use the specified trace inner product. The stop test measures r_1^{m+1}−r_1^m and returns λ_1^{m+1}; budget_exhausted carries no tolerance certificate.
The added-mass recurrence is stipulated only for positive scalar masses, starts at n=0, and is not asserted to describe general fluid-structure schemes.

load_bearing.statement: On finite-dimensional real spaces X_i=I_i⊕Λ with dim Λ≥1, self-adjoint positive-definite M_i,A_i define B_i=Δt⁻¹M_i+A_i. Interior elimination gives outward flux q_i=S_iλ_i−f_i; common trace and flux balance give (S_1+S_2)λ=f_1+f_2.

For a self-adjoint positive-definite block operator B=((K,C),(C*,D)) on a finite-dimensional real inner-product direct sum I⊕Λ, K and S=D−C*K⁻¹C are positive definite, and ⟨Sz,z⟩=min_x ⟨B(x,z),(x,z)⟩ for every z∈Λ.

An ALE map is C² on a neighborhood of the reference space-time closure, each A_t is an orientation-preserving neighborhood diffeomorphism, J=det(DξA_t)>0, and w_m(x,t)=∂tA_t(A_t⁻¹(x)); the specified reference and transported boundary presentations are required.
For the ALE moving-domain map, ∂tJ(ξ,t)=J(ξ,t) div_x w_m(A_t(ξ),t).

For every admissible input the finite procedure returns mesh_crossing without a state if some new Jacobian is nonpositive, or success with a unique array otherwise. Successful steps conserve periodic weighted mass and preserve every constant state without a CFL condition.

For the specified positive Schur operators and α>0, all Robin solves exist uniquely and the algorithm terminates within M passes. Its unique fixed point corresponds to the monolithic trace; incoming errors propagate by R_2R_1 with norm bound q=||R_1||||R_2||<1. A passing stop test certifies ||λ_1^{m+1}−λ_*||≤ε.

alerts.finding: Step 2.1 says: “every $2\times2$ block collapses to the scalar block $[a]$.” Setting b=0 makes the displayed 2×2 block equal to aI₂, retaining two coordinates; [a] denotes a 1×1 block. The subsequent diagonality and eigenbasis conclusions remain valid, but this block-size wording is inaccurate.
